Stage 3 cell-channel batch (2026-09-17) briefly set maximum=32, inferring it from CellVol/CellWireRes/CellConWireRes all spanning channel indices 0-31 -- REVERTED (targeted correction, same day, user-directed): that fact proves the protocol's REGISTER MAP allocates 32 channel slots (protocol channel capacity), it does NOT prove CellCount's own register accepts values up to 32. Re-searched both the official PDF and the V2 workbook specifically for CellCount's own documented valid range and found neither states one (PDF: no narrative range text near the register, only an unrelated example value "15" in the command-example table; workbook: description column has no range, its "приклад значення" column "16" is this deployed unit's own observed/configured value, not a stated maximum -- see this field's own workbook evidence citation, already graded observed_decoded_value, not a range claim). maximum=16 restored -- itself ALSO not a confirmed protocol-wide maximum, just this deployed unit's own observed value (same status it always had). Three genuinely separate facts, kept distinct: (1) protocol channel capacity is 32 (evidenced via CellVol/CellWireRes/CellConWireRes 0-31 -- a real fact about the register MAP, independent of CellCount's own range); (2) this deployed unit's operational support ceiling is 16 (resolve_topology's own MAX_CELL_CHANNELS, batterylifepo4.yaml, unchanged); (3) CellCount's own confirmed valid range remains genuinely UNKNOWN -- neither 16 nor 32 should be read as a proven protocol maximum for this specific register. No evidence citation was added or removed on this field for this correction (still the same 4 pre-existing citations as before the batch) -- the goal is not to game the verification-status/effective-access derivation cascade either way, only to state plainly what is and is not actually confirmed.

Firmware coalesces 0x1290/0x1294/0x1298 into one 12-byte Modbus read for atomicity (implementation detail, not a protocol structure) — modeled here as three separate protocol registers, matching the upstream reference's own per-register table. The value the UI shows as 'total voltage' is g_total_voltage_v, a non-register calculated field derived from this raw read.
Sign convention audited in batterylifepo4.yaml: positive = charging, negative = discharging.

Wire encoding is signed INT32 (S32), confirmed independently by the official PDF (p.11, 'SOCCapRemain' row, distinguished from neighboring UINT32 rows in the same table), the verified V2 workbook, and the upstream project's own comment — batterylifepo4.yaml's value_type was corrected from U_DWORD to S_DWORD to match. A prior pass had instead changed the CANONICAL signedness to unsigned, reasoning that remaining capacity cannot be physically negative; that conflated wire signedness with domain bounds, which are tracked separately here (minimum/maximum stay 0/2000 Ah — the physical range is still non-negative, only the wire's two's-complement interpretation changed).
